problems.title: Two Sum
problems.description: Given an array of integers and a target value, find the two distinct positions whose values add up to the target. Return their indices.
constraints: Assume exactly one valid pair exists.
The same array element cannot be used twice.
problems.trigger: Need to find a complementary value while scanning the array once.
problems.aha: Instead of searching for the partner after seeing a number, store previously seen values so the complement lookup is O(1) average.
approach: Create a hash map from value to its index.
Scan the array from left to right.
For each value x, compute target - x.
If the complement is already in the map, return its index and the current index.
Otherwise store x and continue.
commonMistakes: Checking the map after inserting the current value.
Using nested loops when a hash map gives linear expected time.
followUps: What changes if the array is sorted?
How would you handle multiple valid pairs?
staffInsights: The hash map trades memory for latency. In a distributed setting, partitioning by value would be difficult because the complementary lookup needs shared state.

problems.title: Valid Parentheses
problems.description: Determine whether a string containing bracket characters is correctly nested and every closing bracket matches the most recent unmatched opener.
constraints: Input contains only bracket characters for this exercise.
problems.trigger: The most recent unmatched opening bracket must be matched first.
problems.aha: Nested matching is last-in-first-out, which is exactly the behavior of a stack.
approach: Create a stack for opening brackets.
Map each closing bracket to its matching opener.
Push opening brackets.
For a closing bracket, verify that the stack top is the expected opener.
Return true only when the stack is empty at the end.
commonMistakes: Forgetting to check an empty stack before pop.
Returning true without verifying that all openers were closed.
followUps: How would you support wildcard brackets?
Can you validate a streaming input?
staffInsights: A streaming validator can process arbitrarily large input without storing the full string; only unmatched openers need to remain in memory.

problems.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
problems.description: Given daily prices, choose one day to buy and a later day to sell to maximize the resulting profit.
constraints: Only one buy and one sell are allowed.
The sell must occur after the buy.
problems.trigger: At each price, the best previous buy is simply the minimum price seen so far.
problems.aha: You do not need to remember every candidate buy day; keep only the minimum price and the best profit so far.
approach: Initialize the minimum price to infinity and best profit to zero.
Scan prices from left to right.
Update the minimum price.
Compute today's profit using the minimum prior price.
Keep the maximum profit.

solutions.python:
def maxProfit(prices: list[int]) -> int:
    min_price = float('inf')
    best = 0
    for price in prices:
        min_price = min(min_price, price)
        best = max(best, price - min_price)
    return best

commonMistakes: Allowing the buy day to occur after the sell day.
followUps: What changes if multiple transactions are allowed?
What if a transaction fee is charged?
staffInsights: The one-pass invariant is simple and robust. In a streaming analytics system, the same state can be maintained without retaining the full price history.

problems.title: Valid Anagram
problems.description: Determine whether two strings contain exactly the same characters with the same frequencies.
problems.trigger: Same multiset of characters means equal frequency for every character.
problems.aha: Count occurrences rather than comparing positions.
approach: If lengths differ, return false.
Build a frequency map from the first string.
Subtract counts using the second string.
Reject if a character is missing or over-consumed.
Return true when all counts balance.
commonMistakes: Sorting both strings when linear counting is sufficient.
followUps: How would you solve it with a fixed alphabet?
How would you process very large strings in chunks?
staffInsights: For a bounded alphabet, the frequency structure is effectively constant-sized. For large Unicode domains, memory depends on the number of distinct symbols.

problems.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
problems.description: Find the maximum length of a contiguous substring in which every character appears at most once.
constraints: The answer must be a contiguous substring.
problems.trigger: Need the longest contiguous region satisfying a uniqueness constraint.
problems.aha: Maintain a window that is always valid; when a duplicate appears, move the left boundary past the previous occurrence.
approach: Maintain a left boundary and a map from character to its latest index.
Scan the right boundary across the string.
When a duplicate appears inside the current window, move left forward.
Update the latest index for the current character.
Track the maximum window length.
commonMistakes: Resetting the whole window when a duplicate appears.
followUps: How would you return the actual substring?
How would the problem change if up to K duplicates were allowed?
staffInsights: The key invariant is that the active window remains valid. This pattern generalizes well to streaming systems where only a bounded active state is required.
